AI & Productivity

AI Features

AI-powered task creation, voice dictation, text enhancement, and an intelligent co-worker built into your workflow.

For tools and limits, see What AI chat can do.

AI is woven through every part of Hypertask — create tasks, filter your board, smart-label workloads, and manage daily operations without leaving the workflow you already use.

  1. AI-assisted task creation
  • Click AI in the top-right corner of any board, open the Ask Hypertask AI panel, and describe a task in plain English.
  • AI parses the description and creates a task pre-assigned to you with a title, description, and relevant tags (task types, priorities, area).
  • Review the generated task before saving; edit fields or refine the prompt and generate again.
  1. Prompt-based filtering
  • In the Board Filter, type natural-language constraints like:
  • show me top-priority bugs
  • tasks assigned to Valentin and due this week
  • Use combinations such as high priority and not blocked, and press Enter to apply.
  1. Smart labels
  • Open a label (or the Manage Tags screen) and create a new label marked as a smart label.
  • In the "Smart label — AI keeps this label on matching tasks" field, define which tasks should carry it, for example:
  • backend issue, involves DB, high impact
  • Save; AI immediately classifies the board up to 500 existing tasks and adds the label to matches. Smart labels show a sparkle icon in label lists.
  • New tasks are classified when created; edited tasks are re-classified when title or description change; updating the prompt re-runs classification for the entire board.
  1. AI usage without a signed-in user
  • AI usage can now be recorded and stored as usage tracks even when calls don't originate from a signed-in user.
  • This allows external agents or systems invoking the AI APIs to function without requiring active authentication, while still producing usage records available to admins.
  1. Batch-powered background workloads
  • Background smart labels and other AI classification runs that involve many tasks are routed to Anthropic's Batch API at half price, allowing cost-efficient processing at scale.
  • Matching tasks receive their labels automatically; activity is logged in the task activity feed.
  • AI writes a compact representation of your content and sends it to the embed service, which can reject very long or empty text or refuse very long or empty text. On these failures, the upsert silently rotates the text and upserts without final vectors instead of failing, so comments and pages remain searchable with the relevant tags even when vectors aren't generated.
  • You don't see extra UI for this—it happens invisibly in the background with consistent results.
  1. AI Chat suggestions for tickets
  • Open AI Chat in a ticket panel to get context-aware suggestions tailored to that ticket's specific information.
  • Previously, suggestions could be generic or fail entirely when the server returned "No output generated"; Haiku 5.5 now returns proper suggestions that match the ticket context.
  1. Faster agent task lists
  • AI agents are now much quicker to load their task lists, especially after server warm-up.
  • Previously slow database reads that fetched task lists have been optimized: the slowest 5% of calls improved from ~129 ms down to ~40 ms. The improvement consistently benefits agents on both warm and cold servers, making AI-driven workflows feel far more responsive.
  1. AI Chat histories
  • A spinner marks chats that are replying. The sidebar header and conversation list show it. Each chat keeps its own indicator. It disappears when replying finishes, fails, or stops.
  • Open AI Chat from the right rail or press Ctrl/Cmd + I to see a list of conversations.
  • In the full-screen chat view (desktop), the history list pages as the window resizes, and you scroll to load more older chats. Pick or filter from that list to open a chat.
  • On mobile, the list is limited; tap an entry to open its history.
  • The docked chat always shows your most recent chats inline; use the full-screen view for history navigation.
  • Drag the desktop chat edge to resize. Your account remembers this width in this browser.
  • Closing, reloading, and changing boards keep your choice. A narrow window temporarily reduces the displayed width. Widening restores your choice.
  1. Comment summaries preserve open questions
  • When AI summarizes your comments, it now accurately reflects whether questions have been answered or remain unresolved.
  • Comment summaries display Open: ... for unanswered questions instead of inventing an answer, and retain "still unresolved" language when appropriate.
  1. Bulk archiving avoids server errors
  • Agents that attempt to archive many tasks see a clear refusal message instead of a server crash.
  • An earlier incident had agents trying to archive 31 Done tickets per day, triggering a 500 error. The fix now returns a direct not allowed response, keeping workflows smooth and errors visible for observers.

Run chats together

Start a reply, then open another chat. Each chat replies independently. There is no two-chat limit. Existing usage limits still apply.

Follow-ups wait only for their own chat. They send in order, even while you read another chat. Select Stop in a chat to stop that reply; other chats keep running.

Keep a conversation across tickets

Pin AI chat open in its menu, then open another ticket. Your selected conversation and earlier messages stay in the sidebar. New messages use the ticket you are viewing as context.

Select New chat to start a separate conversation. Creating a ticket with the task writer puts that ticket's own introduction in the conversation you have open; it never opens the chat for you.

Image generation removed

Hypertask no longer generates new images. Existing images and uploads remain unchanged.

Image generation is absent from team settings. Check Settings → Team → Default models and AI features. The Ctrl+K image generation shortcut was removed. Image model mentions were also removed.

Where AI appears

AreaWhat AI does

Board filteringUnderstands natural-language constraints and builds dynamic filters.
Smart LabelsKeeps labels on tasks that match your AI prompt; changes to tasks or the prompt trigger reclassification.
AI ChatGlobal assistant for questions, summarization, and quick actions, with full-screen history paging.
Ticket AI suggestionsProvides context-specific suggestions in ticket panels that mirror the ticket's subject and related data.
Bulk AI workloadsHeavy classification runs use the Batch API to handle large boards efficiently; background jobs go through Anthropic's half-price Batch endpoint. Usage is recorded as usage tracks regardless of whether a signed-in user is present.

When the chat opens and closes

The AI chat stays where you put it.

  • It opens when you open it, and closes when you close it. Moving between tickets, boards, My Tasks and the inbox leaves it as it was.
  • It keeps the same conversation while you move around a team. A new ticket no longer starts a new thread behind your back.
  • Creating a task leaves it as it was too. A closed chat stays closed; an open one stays open.
  • Reloading a tab keeps the state you left: open stays open, closed stays closed.

Task creation with AI writer

  1. Open the New Task box — Use Ctrl+J on desktop or Cmd+J to open the New Task creator from boards, the inbox, or any view. On the Tasks page, click New Task in the toolbar.

To change the destination, press Ctrl+Shift+B (or Cmd+Shift+B on Mac). The board picker lists recently visited boards first, then sorts ties alphabetically. It remembers board visits in this browser. Search for a board and press Enter, or click its name.

  1. Describe your task — Enter a brief description of the work you need done. You can type directly or let AI expand your ideas. The model chip under the note shows the model that will write the task: click it to pick another model or effort level, or use Reset to default to go back to the board's default.
  1. Let AI write the task — Reviews your inputs and generates a complete, structured task with a title, description, priority, and relevant tags. AI respects your board's templates and style when available.
  1. Review and refine — Edit any field in the generated task. You can press Ctrl+K (desktop) or Cmd+K (Mac) in the description area to refine the AI's work, regenerate, or add more detail.
  1. Save the task — When you're satisfied, click Create (or Enter) to save the task and add it to the board. The task appears immediately in the appropriate column or section.
  1. Answer the follow-up questions — The new task opens with the AI chat sidebar next to it. Under Questions and ideas for this ticket, it shows up to three one-tap chips based on your original note and your board's rules, such as a next action to take, a job to split out, or an open decision to settle. Click one to send it in the same chat. When nothing fits, no chips appear.

Creating tickets through AI Chat

Ask AI Chat to create a ticket. Its saved link appears before writing finishes. Open it while its description is being written. The finished title, description, priority and size follow. Saved title or description edits stop automatic replacement. If writing fails, the saved ticket remains. Chat tells you its description is unfinished. Finish that ticket instead of creating another.

AI writer failure reasons

Fix When the AI writer fails to generate a task, the Ctrl+J New Task box and the AI Task Writer now show you the real reason for the failure instead of hiding it. Your note is still saved as a task, so you don't lose your work:

  • Error messages displayed — Common errors like quota limits, missing context, or prompt format issues show explainable messages.
  • Task created anyway — Your original description or note is preserved as a task, so you can retry AI later or edit it manually.
  • Applies everywhere — This fix covers task creation from boards, the inbox, and when editing task descriptions.

If AI generation is not available (for example, your team has not configured an AI key), the text you entered appears without modification, keeping your workflow uninterrupted.

AI Task Writer

The AI Task Writer is a prompt-based task creation flow that generates complete, shippable tickets from paste inputs.

How it works today

The Task Writer uses the board's saved custom instructions whenever you write a ticket with Ctrl+J compose, ask AI chat to create a ticket, or use the CLI/MCP task writer.

  • Board format — Keeps the section layout shared by past tickets, such as Problem, Hypothesis, Control, Variation, and a scoring section, while keeping each section short.
  • Custom fields — Fills the board's Number, Select, Text, Date, and Checkbox fields when the instructions or past tickets show what to use. For example, a score field can match the score in the title. Values that do not fit the field are skipped.

It also uses search to find related tickets instead of inventing them.

Using the Task Writer

  • From a board: Ctrl+J / Cmd+J and select Create with AI — Task Writer.
  • From the command palette: Ctrl+K — search for "Task Write" and select it.
  • From a task: Click the AI icon in the task header and select Task Writer.

After the Task Writer generates a draft, you can refine it just like any other AI-generated comment or description.

When Ctrl+J or AI chat writes a task description or comment that references an uploaded image or image link, the image appears inline in the text by default. Ask for "attachment only" or "link only" to keep it as an attachment or link instead.

Included AI allowance

Free gets a small starter AI allowance on fast budget models. Pro includes more AI on managed models with no keys needed. BYOK uses your own model keys. Owners and board admins see percent used in Settings > AI Usage.

Background AI, including smart labels and summaries, counts toward the same allowance as interactive AI when it uses Hypertask's key.

Calls using your own provider key do not use the included allowance.

When the included allowance is reached, further calls on Hypertask's key are refused. Your own-key calls can continue.

Demo chat requires an active demo guest session. If prompted, start the demo again to keep chatting.

When AI is not available

Behavior change AI features now show clear guidance when a team does not have an AI key configured. Previously, teams without an AI key would see server errors when trying to use AI in agents or the CLI. Now, users receive a concise message directing them to add an AI key through the Appearance & AI Models settings page:

"AI features require an AI key. Configure your AI key in Appearance & AI Models."

This applies to AI-powered task creation, filters, smart labels, and agent workflows that invoke AI.

Settings

  • Choose your preferred AI model in the Appearance & AI Models settings page. Different models may produce different responses.
  • If a provider rejects your own AI key during chat, the message names that key and tells you to update it in Settings, then AI, then Bring your own key.
  • Adjust leniency of AI-assisted task creation in the same settings area if you prefer more precise or broader suggestions.
  • Smart label accuracy can be tuned by sharpening or relaxing your prompt; see the "How it stays current" details in the Smart Labels reference.

Smart labels and prompts are a best-effort AI signal. They do not substitute for human review. Ensure your prompt manages edge cases or exceptions directly, for example: "NOT: schema changes on branches not yet merged."

Use smart labels together with filters and saved views to create reusable patterns for recurring workloads (e.g., on-call issues, quick fillers, enterprise integrations).
